newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANI says Holter loss narrows.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANI says Holter loss narrows.

text.p: Australian National Industries Ltd (ANI) said on Tuesday losses before interest and tax from its troubled environmental engineering unit Holter narrowed to A$14.3 million in the six months to December 31 from A$18.9 million.
ANI said the principal cause of the Holter loss was a further delay in the completion of its waste-to-energy plant in Madrid which is now scheduled for completion in April 1997.
The company said losses were also experienced by Holters ABT waste-to-energy business and from the HIT Holter Industrie-Tecknic engineering operation.

"Partially offsetting these losses, were after tax profits of A$4.2 million generated by Holter's waste energy business, SHW Holter Wassertechnik (SHW), in the two months following it becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary of ANI from November 1, 1996," ANI said in a statement.
ANI acquired the remaining 50 percent of SHW in January for DM65.5 million after joint venture partner Saarberg exercised its right of rescission to sell its stake to ANI.
"The SHW business is the best managed and most profitable business within the Holter operation and the waste water treatment industry has very good prospects for further growth," the company said.

ANI said that as a part of its overall strategy to no longer operate a wholly-owned subsidiary in the environmental engineering industry, it had engaged a merchant bank to advise it in relation to the divestment of some Holter assets.
"The bank is now in the process of arranging for the sale of SHW via an international tender," ANI said.

The company said other steps taken in reducing its exposure to this business included the sale of Holter's 50 percent interest in SHU Saarberg-Holter Umwelttechnik GmbH to Saarbergwerke AG and its 50 percent interest in UTR Umwelt-Technologie und Recycling GmbH and the Holter ABT Mining Filter business to Ruhrkohle AG.
ANI said it was also offering Holter ABT's industrial filter business and coal preparation business, the Polho coal treatment plant and HIT Holter Industrie-Technik business for sale.
Installation of new senior management and an improved regime of cost management, mainly through programmed staff reductions was also being undertaken, ANI said.
ANI shares closed at A$1.25 on Monday, down three cents on the day.
